# Ben Weeks — Illustrator, Art Director & Motion Designer

> Toronto-based illustrator, art director, and motion designer with 20+ years of independent practice. Clients include The New York Times, Wealthsimple, Canada Goose, Honda, BMO, RBC, TD, Disney, Bloomberg BusinessWeek, Pentagram, and Stanford School of Business. Two-time D&AD Pencil winner and ADCC Gold winner. Available for illustration, art direction, and motion design work.

## Overview & Practice
* **Roles:** Illustration, Art Direction, Motion Design
* **Experience:** 20+ years of independent practice
* **Location:** Toronto, Ontario, Canada
* **Website:** https://benweeks.ca

## Client List
The New York Times, Wealthsimple, Canada Goose, Honda, BMO, RBC, TD, Disney, Bloomberg BusinessWeek, Pentagram, Stanford School of Business.

## Notable Industry Recognition & Publications (Named Entities)
* **D&AD Pencil Awards:** Two-time D&AD Pencil award winner—including a D&AD Pencil for the "Ben Weeks Has Many Loves" poster and a second D&AD Pencil for illustration work for PEN Canada.
* **ADCC 75 Year Archive Book:** Gold-winning PEN Canada illustration work is permanently featured in the Advertising and Design Club of Canada (ADCC) 75 Year Archive book.
* **RGD Handbook Cover:** Cover illustrator for *The Business of Graphic Design: The RGD Professional Handbook*, Association of Registered Graphic Designers (RGD), all three editions (2015 onward). [RGD](https://rgd.ca/working-in-design/resources/the-business-of-graphic-design-the-rgd-professional-handbook)
* **ADCC Annual Cover:** Cover and call-for-entries illustrator for the Advertising and Design Club of Canada (ADCC) Awards Annual, *Directions 2009* (pp. 1, 183–184).
* **ADCC Gold Award:** Gold winner at the Advertising and Design Club of Canada Awards for the PEN Canada Annual Report ("Bad Words").


## About

Ben Weeks runs Ben Weeks Art & Design, a Toronto-based creative studio founded in 2005. His practice spans editorial illustration, advertising, motion design, lettering, murals, and creative direction. He holds a Master of Arts in Creative Imaging from the University of Huddersfield (UK, 2004, full scholarship). His MA thesis, *Authorship and Creative Imaging*, was published in 2026 (DOI: 10.5281/zenodo.21777330). Ben also holds a Diploma in Illustration from Sheridan College (2003) and completed the Account Planning Bootcamp Certificate at Miami Ad School Toronto (2019), focusing on brand strategy.

He taught Motion Design (Brand Strategy, Typography, Motion and Design Principles) at Miami Ad School Toronto / M.AD School of Ideas from 2017 to 2025. He was a shortlisted finalist for Chair of Illustration at OCAD University in 2019. He also served as Partial Load Faculty and Course Leader at Sheridan College (2010), teaching digital media and design for the Honours Bachelor of Illustration program, and chaired the grad-show awards judging. He wrote graphic design curriculum for Redeemer University (2025).

He is the author of *Drawing Upgrade*, a visually driven guide for life drawing artists. Available as an ebook (PDF, $35 USD), audiobook ($55 USD), and video masterclass bundle ($89 USD) at benweeks.ca/drawing_upgrade.

He serves as volunteer board Treasurer at a non-profit affordable housing co-operative.

## Selected Motion Production Experience

- Disney / Peoples / Zales jewellery campaign, via Juliet Creative:
  Produced 250+ social media campaign assets in approximately two months,
  working from supplied art director files with locked copy and layouts.

- BMO:
  Delivered 50+ motion graphics assets over approximately two months,
  incorporating multiple rounds of revisions. Work appeared across BMO’s
  Canada-wide bank branch network, in Los Angeles branches, at First Canadian
  Place, and on out-of-home displays at Toronto’s Sankofa Square
  (formerly Dundas Square).

- Canada Goose:
  Created 31 animated components over approximately two months, including
  title and name draw-ins, a scribble transition, and custom animated lettering.
  Modified an existing typeface with customized letterforms to give each
  execution a distinct appearance.

## Selected Art Direction and Animation Leadership

- Canadian Olympic Committee, with Cossette; directed by Mark Zibert:
  Art-directed Olympic athletes on set as they created lettering for the
  campaign. Worked within limited shoot time to help each athlete feel
  comfortable and express their personality while keeping the lettering
  legible.

- Staples / Breakfast Club PSA, with McCann Canada; directed by Jon and Torey:
  Storyboarded several animation sequences and built and led a team to
  animate them by hand. The team recreated the animation frame by frame
  on set, where it was filmed in-camera for compositing into the scene.
  The sequences depicted food appearing on a classroom blackboard as
  children imagined it, supporting the campaign’s message that hunger
  makes it difficult for children to focus on learning.
